content.text:
No zstd CLI, no python zstandard module. But Node's zstd works for single frames. I can split the multi-frame stream: zstd frames start with magic `28 b5 2f fd`. I can scan the buffer for the magic bytes and decompress each frame separately! Frames can appear at any offset; but the magic sequence may coincidentally appear inside compressed data (rare). Simple approach: split at each occurrence of the 4-byte magic, trying each segment; decompress segments; if a segment fails, try merging with the next (since false positives possible).

Let me implement:
1. Find all indices of magic.
2. For each index i, take buf[i..nextIndex) and try zstdDecompressSync; if fails, extend to the following magic boundary, etc.

That should recover the full JSONL. Then search for markers.

Let me test on the largest file first, then scan all recent sessions for "reducedQPilotAnchor"/"S1960QPilotAnchor"/"## S1894". Given 235MB compressed across ~104 files, decompression may take a while but manageable (zstd is fast; ~1-2s per 1MB file → ~200s; risky for the 120s default; set timeoutMs 300000).

Actually, is this the best use of time? The recovery of the ledger is valuable but my primary deliverable is done. Also the parent should be notified ASAP about the ledger incident. Let me send the message to the parent now (with the S1977 result + incident + recovery plan), then continue recovery.

Actually — messages don't end my turn, and the parent benefits from early notice. Let me send a concise message now, then continue the recovery attempt.

Wait: sending a message requires the message content; fine.

Let me first send the message, then do the recovery.
